title: Colour-equivalent approximations are marked operadic weak equivalences
statement:
Use symmetric infinity operads, inert markings and the categorical-pattern model category $\mathsf M$ of [lem-coef-symmetric-operadic-fibration-recognition], and quasicategories and inner/cocartesian fibrations of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Let $p:P\to N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ be a small symmetric infinity operad. A pointed map is active if only its basepoint maps to the basepoint.

Call a categorical fibration $g:D\to P$ an approximation when (i) for every $d$ over $\langle n\rangle$ and every colour projection $\rho_i$ there is a locally $pg$-cocartesian edge $d\to d_i$ over $\rho_i$ whose image in $P$ is inert, and (ii) every active edge $z\to g(d)$ in $P$ admits a $g$-cartesian lift with target $d$. Locally cocartesian means cocartesian in the pullback over the specified edge. A coherent functor $f:C\to P$ is an approximation if, over $P$, it factors as a categorical equivalence followed by such a categorical fibration. Mark an edge of $C$ exactly when its image in $P$ is inert, and write $C^{\mathrm{in}/P}$ for this marked object.

If $f:C\to P$ is an approximation and its colour-fibre functor $C\times_{N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)}\{\langle1\rangle\}\to P_{\langle1\rangle}$ is an equivalence, then the marked map
$$f:C^{\mathrm{in}/P}\longrightarrow P^{\mathrm{in}}$$
is a weak equivalence in $\mathsf M$. This assertion includes arbitrary coherent approximations, without a categorical-fibration hypothesis on $f$ itself.

source.place: Higher Algebra (2017), Definitions 2.3.3.6 and 2.3.3.25, Lemma 2.3.3.10 (approximations are weak approximations) and Theorem 2.3.3.23(1) together with the weak-equivalence test in Proposition 2.1.4.6; also the consequence recorded in Remark 2.3.3.27 after Theorem 2.3.3.26. The unary equivalence hypothesis of the preceding theorem is retained when using Remark 2.3.3.27. Read online on 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-operadic result.
